name: Kartu Charge Danamon American Express Gold

fees.condition: converting points to airline miles or hotel points needs the Frequent Traveller Option at a further Rp 250.000 a year

rules.name: Half a point more, up to one times the monthly limit

welcomeBonus: Up to 210.000 Membership Rewards points has been offered on this card. The amount and the conditions move between campaigns, so nothing is modelled.
notes: This is the charge card, sometimes called RCP Gold: no preset spending limit, no minimum payment, and an annual fee of Rp 1.200.000. Danamon also issues a Danamon American Express Gold credit card at Rp 350.000, which is a separate entry. The two share the Membership Rewards programme but earn differently.

Earning is 1,5 Membership Rewards points per Rp 2.500 up to one times the monthly limit, and 1 point per Rp 2.500 above it. That is written as a base of 1 with half a point stacked on top, the stacked half capped at the card's limit, so the two rates fall out of one cascade.
The rate is the same at home and abroad, and the same in every category. There is no foreign-currency or category bonus on this card.

The cap is read from the card's own credit limit when the entry is applied. A charge card has no preset limit, so the figure to record is whatever monthly limit Danamon has set for the holder. If no limit is recorded the uplift runs uncapped and every rupiah earns 1,5, which overstates a month that goes past the limit.

Insurance premiums, cash advances, money transfers, balance conversions, instalment conversions and cancelled transactions earn nothing. Insurance is matched by category; the rest are matched on the description, so a cash advance or an instalment is only recognised when the description says so.

Converting points to airline miles or hotel points needs the Frequent Traveller Option, a separate subscription of Rp 250.000 a year. The app treats the partners as always available and does not charge the subscription, so a holder without FTO cannot actually transfer at all.

No source could be read directly. Bank Danamon's site, its RIPLAY, americanexpress.com, PinterPoin and IndoMiles are all unreachable from here, so every figure comes from search summaries of those pages rather than the pages themselves. Treat the whole entry as unverified until the RIPLAY is checked.
Not modelled: Priority Pass lounge visits twice a year and the travel insurance cover. Neither pays points.

Six conversions were read off the cardholder's own Frequent Traveller Option screens: 6.000 points for 1.000 KrisFlyer miles, 9.000 for 1.000 Asia Miles, 4.500 for 500 GarudaMiles, 50.000 for 5.000 Enrich miles, 7.000 for 1.250 Hilton Honors points and 6.250 for 990 Marriott Bonvoy points. Reduced, those are 6:1, 9:1, 9:1, 10:1, 28:5 and 625:99, and every block reproduces exactly from its reduced ratio.

At the base rate of 1 point per Rp 2.500 that makes a KrisFlyer mile Rp 15.000, a GarudaMile or Asia Mile Rp 22.500, an Enrich mile Rp 25.000, a Hilton point Rp 14.000 and a Bonvoy point Rp 15.783. While spending stays under the monthly limit the 1,5 rate takes a third off each: a KrisFlyer mile costs Rp 10.000, which is what makes this card worth its fee.

These replace ratios of 8 points a KrisFlyer mile and 12 an Asia Mile, which earlier versions of this entry and its credit-card sibling derived from reported per-mile rupiah figures. The derivation was wrong in both cases; the cardholder's screens are what the entry now records.

The figures given are minimums, and the step past the minimum is not known. The entry treats each minimum as the step too, so a balance converts in whole blocks and a remainder waits. If the bank in fact allows finer increments past the minimum, a conversion is understated.
AirAsia BIG points are the one Frequent Traveller Option partner left without a ratio, so an estimate for them shows nothing.
